nodes.title: Omni  —  refs 1-8 = subjects, ref 9 = background plate
Note: how to run this
widgets_values:
## FastH3 Omni (seriesmith)

FastVideo's 8-step distilled H3 reference model: no turbo LoRA, CFG 1, shift 12 (video) / 3 (audio), VSA sparse attention at 10%.

One shot per queue. Nothing chains, so shots render in any order and a bad
shot is re-queued alone.

### How it runs
seriesmith renders this workflow: for each take it fills **Shot Loader** with
the shot (its frozen shotlist and its files, uploaded) and **Save Take** with
the take, then sends it to the backend. Edits to anything else here (sampler,
LoRA, attention, VAEs) carry into seriesmith's renders while this copy is
saved under this name.

### Resolution
`1344x768` is H3's native canvas and both axes are multiples of 32.
**1280x720 is not legal** - 720 is not divisible by 32. The loader raises
rather than letting H3 fail. Crop to 1344x756 and upscale at conform for
true 16:9 delivery.

### Reference sockets
- `ref_image_0..7` <- the shot's SUBJECTS (up to eight): characters first, then
  props and vehicles, in the order the script lists them (Shot Loader's
  `ref_1`..`ref_3`, then `ref_4`..`ref_8`)
- `ref_image_8` <- the LOCATION plate for this shot, always
In the prompt these are `<Picture 1>`..`<Picture 9>` - **1-based in the
prompt, 0-based on the sockets**.

Character sheets are a **horizontal 4-panel strip** (3/4 body, side, back,
face). `ref_image_size: max` scales the SHORT side to 2048, so a horizontal
strip keeps every panel crisp - a square grid would not. Props and vehicles are
a single clean image on a flat background; they are never panel-cropped.

There is no style reference. Style is carried by every sheet and plate already
- they are all drawn in it - and stated in the prompt text. Slot 9 goes to the
background, which buys layout, palette, lighting direction and depth for THIS
shot, and keeps one location looking like one place across every cut.

`panel_mode` controls reference cost:
- `auto` - full 4-panel strip for a single-character close-up, 3/4+face pair
  otherwise. **Use this.**
- `full` / `pair` / `face` - force it.

Reference cost scales with strip width. Three characters at full 4-panel is
~50M pixels of reference encode per shot; the `pair` crop roughly halves it.

### Audio references
`ref_audio_0..2` carry one clip each. How many are used depends on the policy:
- `clone` -> ONE TIMBRE SAMPLE PER SPEAKER. A two-hander feeds two. Feeding one
  would voice the second character from the first one's sample.
- `dub` / `dub_keep_foley` -> one clip only: the slice of the recorded mix,
  which already contains every voice in the shot.
- `generate` -> none.
Unused sockets receive null. H3 takes at most 3 standalone audio references, so
a clone shot is capped at 3 speakers.

### Audio policy (per shot, from shotlist.json)
- `generate` - no reference fed. H3 invents ambience and foley, and it is
  good at it. The mp4 gets H3's audio.
- `dub` - your recorded line drives lip-sync. The mp4 is written **mute** and
  H3's mix is kept beside it as `_h3.wav`. Lay the clean vocal in at conform.
- `dub_keep_foley` - same, plus Demucs strips the vocal from H3's mix and
  writes `_foley.wav` so you keep the synced foley under your own vocal.
  Needs `pip install demucs`.
- `clone` - a voice sample drives timbre and H3 speaks the line written in
  the prompt's `<d>` tag. No recording session; expect some drift across a
  long episode. Good for the proxy pass and for incidental characters.

### Sampling
4 steps / `euler` / `simple` / LoRA 1.0. SLA stays LAST in the model chain,
wired to both the guider and the scheduler.

If identity slips, in order: raise `panel_mode` to `full`, then try
`res_multistep` (roughly doubles time), then drop `sparsity_ratio` to 0.80.

nodes.title: Note: what H3 gives you
widgets_values:
## Frames are available

`VAEDecode` emits the whole frame batch as IMAGE **before** anything muxes it
into a video. Save Take writes them as a PNG sequence when `save_frames` is
on, and always writes H3's audio separately as `_h3.wav`.

**There is no alpha channel.** H3 outputs opaque RGB with no matte, so
compositing here means grading, effects and titles - not lifting a character
off a background.

Budget ~16-50 GB of PNG per 12-minute episode at 1344x768. Leave
`save_frames` off for shots that need no finishing work.
